full_judgment:
5. The defendant Nos. 1-3 i.e. the Government contested the suit by filling written statement. The learned Additional Assistant Judge, Dhaka by his judgment and decree dated 30.11.89 decreed the suit in favour of the petitioners and declared that inclusion of the house in question as an abandoned property is illegal. Further the case of the petitioners is that behind the knowledge of the petitioners their house in question has been listed in the ka list of abandoned properties published in the official gazette dated 23.9.86 in Serial No. 156 and the petitioners came to know about the listing of their house in the ka list in the last part of October, 1994. As a result the time for filing application before the Court of Settlement expired. In view of the above on 22.10.94 the petitioners submitted an application to Joint Secretary (Abandoned Property) of the Ministry of Housing. Public Works Government of Bangladesh and prayed for releasing the house in question from ka list. 

 10. It appears that the petitioner property was treated as an abandoned property. The petitioners from time to time approached the relevant authorities for releasing the house in question from the list of abandoned properties. The petitioners buying failed to obtain the desired remedy as plaintiffs instituted a Title Suit being No. 170 of 1986 in the Court of the then Munsif, First Court, Dhaka (subsequently the said Title suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 153 of 1989 in the Court of Additional Assistant Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title and that the property is not an abandoned property and it also appears that the suit was in fact pending for hearing before the publication of the lists of die abandoned buildings in the official Gazette on 23.9.86. We have perused section 5(6) of the Abandoned Buildings (supplementary provisions) Ordinance, 1985 wherein it is provided that no list shall include any buildings in respect of which a suit appeal application or other legal proceedings is pending before any Court immediately before the date of publication of the list in the official Gazette in which the vesting in or possession of the Government of the building as abandoned property under the President's Order has been called in question in any manner whatsoever or any prayer has been made for return restoration or transfer of the building by the Government or by any officer or authority subordinate to it to any person. It appears that the petitioners have also annexed to this petition the judgment and decree passed in T.S. 153 of 1989 in favour of the petitioners as Annexure-C. The judgment and decree shows that the Additional Assistant judge. Dhaka passed a decree in favour of the petitioners and against the defendant Nos. 1-3 namely the Government on contest and the declaration of the property in question as abandoned property was held illegal. It also appears that the Government did not file any appeal as against the aforesaid judgment dated 30.11.89 declaring the property as not abandoned property. Therefore that judgment remains binding upon the respondents. Moreover as has already been noticed that the Government bad listed the property as an abandoned property in violation of section 5 sub-section(b) of Ordinance No. LIV of 1985. Since the civil suit was pending in the Court of law in respect of the house in question the Government was not entitled to enlist the same in the list of abandoned buildings.
